subject: Cooking
title: Alcohol Doesn't Fully Cook Off
description: A fast breakdown of Alcohol Doesn't Fully Cook Off for builders.

hook.text: 'Don't worry, the alcohol cooks off.' This comforting phrase is scientifically wrong.

buildup.text: Alcohol boils at 173°F, lower than water. So people assume it evaporates quickly when heated.

discovery.text: USDA studies show that after 30 minutes of simmering, 35% of alcohol remains. After flambéing, 75% stays.

twist.text: To remove virtually all alcohol, food must simmer for over 2.5 hours — far longer than most recipes call for.

climax.text: This matters for recovering alcoholics, pregnant women, and anyone who genuinely needs to avoid alcohol.

punchline.text: Alcohol doesn't vanish in the pan. It just gets quieter.

quiz.question: How much alcohol remains after 30 minutes of simmering?

details.summary: Contrary to popular belief, cooking does not remove all alcohol from food. After 15 minutes of simmering, about 40 percent of the alcohol remains. Even after 2.5 hours, roughly 5 percent persists. Only prolonged baking or flambéing removes most alcohol.
details.whyItMatters: This myth matters for people avoiding alcohol for health, religious, or recovery reasons. Knowing that significant alcohol can remain in cooked food allows informed dietary choices.
takeaways: Flambéing retains about 75 percent of original alcohol content
Two and a half hours of simmering still leaves 5 percent alcohol
The wider the cooking vessel, the faster alcohol evaporates

faq.question: How was alcohol retention in cooking measured?
faq.answer: USDA researchers added known amounts of alcohol to various dishes and measured what remained after different cooking times and methods. The results showed that cooking method, time, temperature, and surface area all affect retention rates significantly.

faq.question: Which cooking methods remove the most alcohol?
faq.answer: Wide, uncovered pans with high heat and long cooking times remove the most. Baking at high temperatures in open dishes is effective. Flambéing, despite the dramatic fire, removes surprisingly little because the flame is brief. Sauces reduced over two hours retain about 5 percent.
